<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

On 2026-10-16 four read-only agents checked every claim in skills/pij (29 markdown files, 2,656 lines, main bb9f0b1) against `pij`/`pij-rs --help` and the Rust code. They found 140 problems: 27 WRONG, 41 STALE, 50 MISSING, 7 BLOAT, 15 UNVERIFIABLE, and about 200 claims that check out. The worst: `link` called unported in six places; a reboot procedure that contradicts revive.rs; role names the CLI refuses; a pair route built on flow-pair and the-flow machinery that no longer exists; TypeScript-daemon behaviour described as current; files that contradict each other; and shipped features (PA prime-active wake, cold-wake guard, canary, decisions, federation) missing. The only gate checks one direction (skill table → shim route table), so nothing catches drift from the CLI back to the skill. Reports: assets/survey/. Rulings for the judgement calls: assets/rulings.md (R1-R7).

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Every claim in skills/pij matches the current CLI and code, or is removed.
- The skill's files agree with each other.
- Shipped behaviour an agent needs is documented in the file whose job it is, by citation where docs/how already covers it.
- A test fails when a CLI verb is added or removed without updating SKILL.md, in both directions.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Changing pij behaviour. This plan changes skill text and two tests only; a skill claim that exposes a code bug becomes an issue, not a fix.
- Creating a governance branch or worktree for pij-fleet (R2).
- Documenting plan 174's double-seat warning before it merges (R7).
- Restructuring the skill's route layout or progressive-disclosure design beyond what the findings need.
